name: Fitzsimons Gateway Apartments
headline: Fitzsimons Gateway is a 210-home, six-story affordable building for households at 30% to 70% AMI at the southeast corner of Colfax Avenue and Peoria Street in Aurora, across from the Anschutz Medical Campus, developed by BMC Investments with Mile High Development on land held in Urban Land Conservancy's community land trust; it won $3,541,829 a year in 2022 federal 4% credit with $39.1M of CHFA private activity bonds.
why_it_matters: It stacks a 99-year land trust ground position, Prop 123 concessionary debt (the first project to break ground using it) and a dozen other financing partners, and took two years from credit award to groundbreaking, a useful case for gap-heavy 4% deals near job centers.

status.label: Built: certificate of occupancy dated 2026-05-14 in Aurora's records; 8609s not yet issued
status.detail: Aurora's building permit for the 210-unit building was issued 2023-11-16, the groundbreaking was 2024-09-17, the structure topped out by July 2025, and Aurora's 2026 certificate of occupancy layer lists 12100 E Colfax Ave with a CO dated 2026-05-14. CHFA still lists the deal on its 2026-09-21 award report, which excludes developments with 8609s issued. No public lease-up figures were found.

next_step: Watch for lease-up news from the developers and for the deal moving to CHFA's 4% completed developments report once 8609s are issued.

background.text: It is BMC Investments' first low-income housing tax credit project and was billed as the launch of a BMC affordable platform targeting more than 500 units in metro Denver over five years.

Urban Land Conservancy owns the land and holds it in its community land trust, which it says ensures at least 99 years of affordability; the building is owned separately (ground lease terms are not public).

The developers described the financing as involving more than a dozen partners; it closed and broke ground in September 2024, about two years after the 2022 credit cycle and ten months after Aurora issued the building permit.
Aurora permit data show later revisions, including a 2025 fire alarm revision adding notification devices for five new ADA units, and access-control permits filed in October 2026.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2022 Round One or Round Two competitive application narratives; it was a rolling 4% bond deal only.

CHFA's 4% award report says it leaves out developments whose IRS Form 8609s have been issued; this deal is still listed on the 2026-09-21 report, so 8609s had not been issued by then (inferred from the report's note).

discrepancies.text: The groundbreaking release describes a 178,000 square foot building, while the topping-out release describes a 239,723 square foot development (the second figure may include the garage).

open_questions: Size of the Prop 123 concessionary loan and of the Division of Housing, City of Aurora, Aurora Urban Renewal Authority and Aurora Housing Authority pieces (a Division of Housing press release that reportedly listed a $5M award no longer loads).
Ground lease terms with Urban Land Conservancy and whether the Aurora Housing Authority holds an ownership interest for a property tax exemption.
Total development cost, equity investor and price, lease-up progress and rents.
Whether the 2026-05-14 certificate of occupancy covers the whole building or is partial.
